intents.reply: FandomVerse is one home for seven fandoms: Anime, Gaming, Movies, TV Shows, K-Pop, Comics and Manga. You can browse titles and characters, watch trailers, check events, save favourites and shop merch.
Hi there! What fandom are you in the mood for today?
You can explore 7 fandom hubs, read articles, browse galleries, watch trailers, check events and releases, save bookmarks and shop merch.
Tell me what you like, for example "I like anime" or "I'm into gaming", and I'll pick a few things for you.
There are community events for every category, from watch nights to dance covers.
All trailers are collected in one place and you can filter them by category or release status.
The releases calendar shows what's coming out month by month.

The shop has FandomVerse tees, hoodies, sweaters, joggers, caps and tote bags, plus fandom merch like Gojo, Sukuna and Goku plushies, Asta and Minecraft Steve figures, an Attack on Titan mug and the One Ring. Add items to your cart and the total updates automatically. The checkout page lets you try entering a delivery address, but it's a showcase only, so nothing is paid for or shipped.
Tap the heart on any title, character, article, video or event to save it. Everything you save shows up on My Favourites, where you can add notes and export the list.
Use the search bar at the top of any page. Results can be filtered by category and content type.
You can reach the FandomVerse team at fandomverse@gmail.com or 07034567890. The contact page also has a message form and a map.
Log in or sign up from the account icon at the top right. It creates a demo profile in your browser with a profile picture, your orders and your comments. There's no real account or password check.
Anytime! Enjoy your fandom time.
Email fandomverse@gmail.com or call 07034567890, or use the form on the contact page.
Head to the community page to see what other fans are talking about.
Open My Favourites and type in the note box under any saved item. Notes stay until you close the browser tab.
On the My Favourites page you can export your list as a .txt file, copy it or print it.
The visitor counter is in the footer of every page.
FandomVerse is completely free to browse. The shop is a showcase, so nothing is charged.
The Characters page lists every profile, and you can filter by category and franchise.

The News page has updates and guides for every title. Each story shows which outlet we fact-checked it with, like Anime News Network or Variety, with a link to the original article. You can also leave a comment at the bottom of any story.
Every category hub has its own image gallery. Click any picture to open it full size.
You can replay the welcome tour any time.

The Trailers & Media page has a Fandom Songs section: Pureojuice's Naruto, Gear 5 and Dragon Ball Z UK drill tracks, plus Sunflower and Hero from the Spider-Man films. They play right here, and you can save them to your Spotify library from the player.
There are actor interviews for Dune, Spider-Verse, Wednesday and One Piece, plus fan interviews. Find them under Interviews on the media page.
FandomVerse was built by a team of five: Isaac John (team lead & front-end), Musah Zaneerah (lead UI/UX), Victory and Zeal Douglas (testing & front-end) and Daramola (testing, data & documentation).
Every news story and article has a comment section at the bottom. Anyone can post by typing a name, or you can log in to comment as your profile.
Open any manga or comic and press Read Books. You'll see official places to read online, like MANGA Plus and the Shonen Jump app, and where to buy the printed volumes on Amazon and Jumia.

Open any movie, game or show and press Download. You'll see the official stores it comes from, like Steam, PlayStation Store, Netflix or Apple TV. If it can't be downloaded, for example trailers or films still in cinemas, it says Download not available. The Downloads page also lets you search every platform at once.

Every category has a podcast you can play right here: Crunchycast for anime, Kinda Funny Gamescast, The Big Picture for movies, The Stranger Things Podcast, The Truly Daebak Show for K-Pop, Marvel's Pull List and Manga Machinations.
